record.paper_title: Some open problems of graph theory.
record.original_question: Determine the minimum possible value of the largest element x_n among all strictly increasing n-term sequences 0 ≤ x_1 < x_2 < ⋯ < x_n of nonnegative integers for which every difference x_j - x_i with 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n is distinct.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. (G. Burosch and J.-M. Laborde) On the minimum value \(\rho\) (n) of \(x_ n\), where \(0\leq x_ 1<x_ 2<...<x_ n\) is a set of non- negative integers with all differences distinct.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A finite set of nonnegative integers $0 \le x_1 < x_2 < \cdots < x_n$ is called a Sidon set (or B_2 set, or Golomb ruler) if all pairwise differences $x_j - x_i$ with $1 \le i < j \le n$ are distinct. Define
$$\rho(n) = \min\{x_n : 0 \le x_1 < x_2 < \cdots < x_n \text{ is a Sidon set of size } n\}.$$
Determine $\rho(n)$ as an exact function of $n$ (equivalently, give a closed-form formula, or matching upper and lower bounds, for the smallest possible value of the largest element of an $n$-element Sidon set of nonnegative integers).
artifact.status_search_result: Determining the exact value of the minimum length of an n-mark Golomb ruler (equivalently, ρ(n) for Sidon sets) is a long-standing open problem. Classical results of Erdős–Turán and Lindström give ρ(n) = n^2 + O(n^{1+ε}) bounds, with the best known being ρ(n) = n^2 + O(n^{0.6})-type, and the conjecture ρ(n) = n^2 + O(1) of Erdős–Turán remains unresolved. Optimal Golomb rulers are known only for small n by computer search; no closed-form formula is known.

status_evidence.title: Analysis of the Golomb Ruler and the Sidon Set Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Optimal Golomb rulers are known only for small n via exhaustive computer search; no closed-form formula for the minimum length is known.
status_evidence.claim: The exact minimum largest element of an n-term Sidon set is unknown in general.

status_evidence.title: Sidon set — Erdős problems
status_evidence.snippet: Multiple Erdős problems on Sidon sets remain open, including precise asymptotics for the minimum largest element.
status_evidence.claim: Determining ρ(n) precisely is still open.
